short_summary: A new restaurant called Dante Mayfair has opened inside the famous Claridge's hotel in London, offering a casual atmosphere and a unique cocktail list.

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.title: Dante Mayfair, Claridge’s, London W1: ‘Are chips ever worth £11? Probably not’ – restaurant review

paragraphs: A famous hotel in London has a brand new restaurant. Dante Mayfair recently opened inside Claridge's on Brook Street. The hotel management hopes the new space will feel like a comfortable living room where guests can relax, enjoy a casual meal, and meet friends.

The restaurant is run by Linden Pride and Nathalie Hudson, a husband-and-wife team from Sydney who previously achieved great success running Caffe Dante in New York. While the site inside Claridge's has changed many times over the years under different famous chefs, the new team aims to bring stability and a welcoming atmosphere to the location.

Visitors entering the hotel can walk through the grand main entrance and enjoy a menu featuring various dishes. Food options include tuna tartare, shrimp cocktails, lobster linguine, pasta, and chicken alla diavola. For dessert, customers can order a sticky toffee doughnut with whisky flambé that catches fire like a firework.

One of the most notable features of Dante Mayfair is its dessert cocktail list. The restaurant uses a special machine to print photographs onto the foam of the drinks using edible ink. Reviewers note that while the food may not win major culinary prizes, the service is warm and the location provides a very handy spot for casual lunches and drinks in the heart of Mayfair.

facts.fact: A new restaurant called Dante Mayfair has opened inside Claridge's hotel in London, created by Linden Pride and Nathalie Hudson.
Linden Pride and Nathalie Hudson previously took over Caffe Dante in New York in 2015.
The menu at Dante Mayfair features dishes like tuna tartare, pasta, chicken alla diavola, and a sticky toffee doughnut with whisky flambé.
The restaurant offers a special dessert cocktail list, including drinks with a photograph printed on top of the foam in edible ink.
